Subject: Discrepancy on March dedicated capacity invoice (INV-789) — VAT double-charged?

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well. We were reconciling March close and spotted a problem with invoice INV-789 (attached). It looks like Redwood charged our account twice for the same dedicated capacity reservation period (March 1–31): the invoice total is €28,800 but our agreed committed amount for the month is €14,400.

Separately, VAT appears to have been applied at 20% on both line items which suggests duplication — we’re showing VAT charged on top of an already-inclusive line item in our accounts payable system. Can you confirm: 1) whether this is a duplicate invoice, and 2) whether you can issue a corrective credit or reissued invoice without the duplicate VAT?

We’d like to close this in this billing period. If you prefer, a credit memo applied to our April statement is fine, otherwise a refund to the credit card on file will work — let us know what you need. I’ve attached our AP remittance note and the invoice PDF.

Thanks,
Amina Qureshi

Forwarding Amina’s note — Starlit AI (D-5921) flagged that INV-789 shows €28,800 vs committed €14,400 for March. They also say VAT appears applied twice. Attached invoice from customer and our copy.

Quick asks: 1) Can finance confirm whether INV-789 was generated twice (system duplicate) or whether two separate charge lines were accidentally summed? 2) Recommendation: full invoice reversal + reissue (preferred if system duplicate) vs goodwill credit (if customer wants expedited close). 3) VAT handling — if we reverse and reissue net of VAT, will that satisfy EU VAT reporting for them?

Preliminary numbers from my check: committed monthly fee = €14,400; invoice total = €28,800 (VAT line = €2,880 on each €14,400 chunk). If we issue a credit memo to remove the duplicate, the net credit should be €14,400 plus the duplicate VAT amount €2,880 (total credit €17,280).

If you need me to route to Tax for a VAT note, I’ll do it — the customer asked for a quick resolution this period. They indicated a credit memo applied to April is okay but prefer a direct refund if that speeds things up.

—Vanessa

Hi Amina — thanks for your patience. We completed our review with Finance and Tax. Summary and resolution below: 

What happened
- Root cause: a duplicate job triggered when we closed a migration window on Mar 31, which caused INV-789 to be issued with duplicated line items. This is a system-side error; your committed amount for the period should have been €14,400.

What we did
- We created credit memo CM-20260401-15 for the full duplicate amount: total credit = €17,280 (that’s €14,400 principal + €2,880 duplicated VAT).
- Credit memo attached: credit-memo-CM-20260401-15.pdf
- We also corrected our accounts and will suppress the duplicate invoice internally so it does not appear in future statements.

Refund vs credit memo
- You indicated in your earlier note that either is acceptable. We have issued the credit memo to be applied to your April statement by default. If you prefer a direct refund to the card on file instead, reply and we’ll issue a payment reversal (expected 5–7 business days for the issuing bank).

VAT documentation
- For EU VAT purposes we created a paired reversal entry and included a VAT reclassification note in the memo. If Starlit needs a signed VAT attestation for local accounting, we can produce an export of the reversal transaction and a short confirmation letter. Please share the VAT registration ID if you’d like that file.

Next steps for you
- Please confirm whether you want the credit applied to April or a refund to the card on file.
- If you need the VAT attestation, reply with the registration ID and we’ll attach it to the credit memo.

I appreciate the flag and we’ll follow up if there’s anything else outstanding.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Accounts Lead | Redwood Inference
